analysis.reply_text:
First, restart your router and modem by unplugging them for about 20 seconds, then plug them back in and wait until all the lights look normal. Next, move closer to the router and, if possible, keep it out in the open, away from walls, metal, and other electronics that can interfere. Then, on your device, forget the Wi-Fi network and reconnect by entering the password again.

After that, check for updates on your device—install any operating system updates and, if available, update your Wi-Fi driver. Next, log into your router’s settings and switch the Wi-Fi channel or try using the 5 gigahertz band if your router supports it, since that can reduce congestion. Finally, update the router firmware if there’s an option for it, and if the drops continue, try a full router reset and set it up again, or contact your internet provider to check for line issues.
